title: Panama Papers — who structures the network

reports.title: How to read this dashboard
reports.query:
Degree is counted live in this database. An intermediary's degree is the number of entities it points to with INTERMEDIARY_OF. An officer's degree is the number of OFFICER_OF links. An entity's degree adds its officers, its intermediaries, and its registered addresses.

Degree centrality on the next line divides by n − 1 = 468,622, the bipartite graph used in the Python notebook.

PageRank and betweenness are on the following pages. This Neo4j server has APOC core and does not have the Graph Data Science library, so those two scores are calculated in notebooks/03_centralities.ipynb (NetworkX) and stored as :CentralityScore nodes. The degree page is an independent Cypher calculation. The notebook checks that the top intermediary degrees match.

reports.title: Entities
reports.query: MATCH (n:Entity) RETURN count(n)

reports.title: Officers
reports.query: MATCH (n:Officer) RETURN count(n)

reports.title: Intermediaries
reports.query: MATCH (n:Intermediary) RETURN count(n)

reports.title: Addresses
reports.query: MATCH (n:Address) RETURN count(n)

reports.title: Highest-degree intermediaries
reports.query:
MATCH (i:Intermediary)-[:INTERMEDIARY_OF]->(e:Entity)
WITH i.name AS name, count(e) AS degree
ORDER BY degree DESC
LIMIT 12
RETURN CASE WHEN size(name) > 32 THEN substring(name, 0, 31) + '…' ELSE name END AS name, degree

reports.title: Highest-degree officers
reports.query:
MATCH (o:Officer)-[:OFFICER_OF]->(e:Entity)
WITH o.name AS name, count(e) AS degree
ORDER BY degree DESC
LIMIT 12
RETURN CASE WHEN size(name) > 32 THEN substring(name, 0, 31) + '…' ELSE name END AS name, degree

reports.title: Highest-degree entities
reports.query:
MATCH (e:Entity)
WITH e,
  COUNT { (e)<-[:OFFICER_OF]-() } +
  COUNT { (e)<-[:INTERMEDIARY_OF]-() } +
  COUNT { (e)-[:REGISTERED_ADDRESS]->(:Address) } AS degree
ORDER BY degree DESC
LIMIT 15
RETURN e.name AS name, e.jurisdiction AS jurisdiction, degree,
       toFloat(degree) / 468622 AS degree_centrality

reports.title: Entities by jurisdiction
reports.query:
MATCH (e:Entity)
WITH e.jurisdiction AS jurisdiction, count(*) AS entities
ORDER BY entities DESC
LIMIT 10
RETURN jurisdiction, entities

reports.title: Share of entities and share of links, by jurisdiction
reports.query:
MATCH (e:Entity)
WITH e, COUNT { (e)<-[:OFFICER_OF]-() } + COUNT { (e)<-[:INTERMEDIARY_OF]-() } + COUNT { (e)-[:REGISTERED_ADDRESS]->(:Address) } AS degree
WITH e.jurisdiction AS jurisdiction, count(*) AS entities, sum(degree) AS degree_sum
WITH sum(entities) AS n, sum(degree_sum) AS d, collect({jurisdiction: jurisdiction, entities: entities, degree_sum: degree_sum}) AS rows
UNWIND rows AS row
RETURN row.jurisdiction AS jurisdiction,
       row.entities AS entities,
       toFloat(row.entities) / n AS share_of_entities,
       toFloat(row.degree_sum) / d AS share_of_links
ORDER BY entities DESC
LIMIT 12

reports.title: Where these scores come from
reports.query: PageRank, damping 0.85, calculated in NetworkX on the same undirected bipartite graph and on the largest component of the capped entity projection. pagerank_x_n in the notebook is PageRank times the number of nodes: 1 is an average node. The bars below are the raw PageRank of the top intermediaries. A second table is the top entities on the projection, which drops connectors above the cap and therefore does not contain the giant intermediaries as nodes.

reports.title: Intermediaries by PageRank
reports.query:
MATCH (n:CentralityScore {graph:'bipartite', measure:'pagerank', kind:'intermediary'})
RETURN CASE WHEN size(n.name) > 32 THEN substring(n.name, 0, 31) + '…' ELSE n.name END AS name, n.score AS pagerank
ORDER BY n.rank

reports.title: Officers by PageRank
reports.query:
MATCH (n:CentralityScore {graph:'bipartite', measure:'pagerank', kind:'officer'})
RETURN n.rank AS rank, n.name AS name, n.extra AS countries, n.score AS pagerank
ORDER BY rank

reports.title: Entities by PageRank, bipartite graph
reports.query:
MATCH (n:CentralityScore {graph:'bipartite', measure:'pagerank', kind:'entity'})
RETURN n.rank AS rank, n.name AS name, n.extra AS jurisdiction, n.score AS pagerank
ORDER BY rank

reports.title: Entities by PageRank, projection component
reports.query:
MATCH (n:CentralityScore {graph:'projection', measure:'pagerank', kind:'entity'})
RETURN n.rank AS rank, n.name AS name, n.extra AS jurisdiction, n.score AS pagerank
ORDER BY rank

reports.title: Sampling
reports.query: Exact betweenness would start a shortest-path search from every node. On the bipartite giant component that is about 311,000 starts, which does not finish in NetworkX. The scores here use 50 random sources on that component and 200 sources on the projection component, seed 0, distances in hops. NetworkX rescales the sample. Read the top of each list. Do not read a small gap between two mid-ranked names as a real difference.

reports.title: Intermediaries by betweenness
reports.query:
MATCH (n:CentralityScore {graph:'bipartite', measure:'betweenness', kind:'intermediary'})
RETURN n.rank AS rank, n.name AS name, n.extra AS countries, n.score AS betweenness
ORDER BY rank

reports.title: Officers by betweenness
reports.query:
MATCH (n:CentralityScore {graph:'bipartite', measure:'betweenness', kind:'officer'})
RETURN n.rank AS rank, n.name AS name, n.extra AS countries, n.score AS betweenness
ORDER BY rank

reports.title: Entities by betweenness, projection component
reports.query:
MATCH (n:CentralityScore {graph:'projection', measure:'betweenness', kind:'entity'})
RETURN n.rank AS rank, n.name AS name, n.extra AS jurisdiction, n.score AS betweenness
ORDER BY rank

reports.title: Orion House and 40 of its entities
reports.query:
MATCH (i:Intermediary)-[r:INTERMEDIARY_OF]->(e:Entity)
WHERE i.name STARTS WITH 'ORION HOUSE SERVICES'
WITH i, r, e
LIMIT 40
RETURN i, r, e

reports.title: Jurisdictions of Orion House clients
reports.query:
MATCH (i:Intermediary)-[:INTERMEDIARY_OF]->(e:Entity)
WHERE i.name STARTS WITH 'ORION HOUSE SERVICES'
RETURN e.jurisdiction AS jurisdiction, count(*) AS entities
ORDER BY entities DESC
LIMIT 8
